examples.en: We raised our juice glasses and made a toast.
I make a toast to the new year with friends.
We all toasted and then ate cake.
The boss suggested that we toast first.

examples.ko: 축하하는 마음으로 건배하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see them toasting with congratulations in their hearts.
Is everyone ready to make a toast?

explain: 건배할 때는 '건배!'나 '위하여!'라고 외쳐요. 무엇을 위해 건배하는지는 '새해를 위하여'처럼 '-을/를 위하여'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Everyone raised their glasses and made a toast.
phrases.nuance_ko: '건배하다'와 뜻이 같고 '건배'를 따로 떼어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 건배하다, with 건배 separated out.

phrases.en: We all shouted "Cheers!" together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잔을 부딪칠 때 외치는 말이에요. '위하여!'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: What you shout when clinking glasses; '위하여!' is also used.

phrases.en: We made a toast to the new year.
phrases.nuance_en: '-을/를 위하여' says what you are toasting to.
phrases.en_equiv: to toast to the new year

explain_en: When toasting, people shout '건배!' or '위하여!'. To say what the toast is for, use '-을/를 위하여', as in '새해를 위하여'.

examples.en: My younger brother learns kendo after school.
Kendo values good manners very much.

examples.ko: 검도가 힘들어도 계속 해 볼 거예요.
examples.en: Even if kendo is hard, I will keep trying.
In kendo you shout loudly.

examples.ko: 검도와 태권도는 모두 몸과 마음을 키워 줘요.
examples.en: Both kendo and taekwondo build body and mind.
My dad is a kendo instructor.

explain: 죽도로 겨루는 무술이에요. 운동하는 곳은 '검도장'이고, 가르치는 사람은 '사범'이라고 해요. '검도를 하다', '검도를 배우다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I do kendo every weekend.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '하다' to say that you do the sport.

phrases.en: The kendo gym is near the school.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the place where kendo is practiced.

phrases.en: The kendo instructor showed me the posture.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who teaches kendo; politely called '사범님'.

explain_en: Kendo is a martial art fought with bamboo swords. The place to practice is a '검도장', and the teacher is called a '사범'. You say '검도를 하다' or '검도를 배우다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling plays the drums in a band.

examples.ko: 드럼 소리가 너무 커서 이웃이 항의했어요.
examples.en: The drum sound was so loud that a neighbor complained.
I attend a drum academy.
This song starts with the drums.
The drums play a big role in keeping rhythm.

examples.ko: 드럼 스틱을 두 개 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two new drumsticks.

explain: 드럼은 '드럼을 치다'처럼 '치다'와 같이 써요. 연주하는 사람은 '드러머'예요. 바이올린은 '켜다', 플루트는 '불다'를 써서 악기마다 동사가 달라요.

phrases.en: The drummer of that band is really cool.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who plays the drums.

phrases.en: I'm going to learn drums during vacation.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 배우다 when you are learning an instrument.

phrases.en: Listening to drum playing makes me excited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드럼을 치는 일 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the act of playing the drums.

explain_en: Drums go with '치다': '드럼을 치다'. A person who plays drums is a '드러머'. Each instrument takes its own verb: the violin uses '켜다' and the flute uses '불다'.

examples.en: We learned the recorder in music class.
The recorder has a clear, light sound.
My younger sibling plays an easy song on the recorder.
I don't know where my recorder is.
I took a recorder test when I was in elementary school.

examples.ko: 리코더에 입을 대고 천천히 불어 보세요.
examples.en: Put your mouth on the recorder and blow slowly.

explain: 리코더는 '불다'와 같이 써서 '리코더를 불다'라고 해요. 피아노는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'처럼 악기마다 짝이 되는 동사가 달라요. '리코더를 연주하다'라고도 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I played the recorder in class.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 불다 because you blow into it.

phrases.en: The sound of the recorder is clear.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the instrument's sound.

phrases.en: My younger sibling plays the recorder.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more formal than 불다.

explain_en: You say 리코더를 불다 (literally, blow the recorder). Each instrument pairs with its own verb: 피아노를 치다 for the piano and 바이올린을 켜다 for the violin. You can also say 리코더를 연주하다.

examples.en: I paint watercolors every weekend.
For watercolors, you mix in a lot of water.
The watercolor hanging on the wall is really pretty.
I painted a seascape in watercolor.
Watercolor paint spreads easily.
I want to learn both watercolor and oil painting.

explain: 물에 푼 물감으로 그리는 그림을 가리켜요. 기름 물감으로 그리는 그림은 '유화'라고 해요. 그린다고 말할 때는 '수채화를 그리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I bought watercolor paints at the stationery shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림을 그리는 재료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the paint used for the art.

phrases.en: The rainy street looks like a watercolor painting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍경이 부드럽고 맑아 보일 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A comparison for soft, gentle-looking scenery.

phrases.en: I'm learning watercolor painting at a culture center these days.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when talking about learning it as a hobby.

explain_en: It refers to a painting made with paint thinned in water. A painting made with oil paint is '유화'. To say you paint one, use '수채화를 그리다'.

examples.en: I can hear organ music in the church.
My older sister knows how to play the organ.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 오르간으로 치면 더 따뜻하게 들려요.
examples.en: That song sounds warmer when played on the organ.
The organ and the piano have similar keyboards.
We had the wedding at a cathedral that has an organ.
I like the piano more than the organ.

explain: 오르간과 피아노는 둘 다 건반이 있지만 소리가 달라요. 오르간도 피아노처럼 '오르간을 치다'라고 말해요. 학교 교실에 있던 작은 건반 악기는 '풍금'이라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 일주일에 한 번 오르간을 배워요.
phrases.en: I learn the organ once a week.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '을/를 배우다' when learning an instrument.

phrases.en: I listened to an organ performance at church.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오르간으로 하는 연주를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a performance played on the organ.

phrases.en: My organ teacher is very kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오르간을 가르치는 사람을 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for the person who teaches you the organ.

explain_en: The organ and the piano both have keyboards, but the sound is different. You say '오르간을 치다', just like '피아노를 치다'. The small keyboard instrument that used to be in classrooms is sometimes called '풍금'.

examples.en: Grandmother sings while playing the janggu.
There is a janggu in the room.

examples.ko: 장구는 양쪽 면을 쳐서 소리를 내요.
examples.en: A janggu makes sound when you hit its two sides.

examples.ko: 학교 동아리에서 장구도 배우고 노래도 불러요.
examples.en: In the school club I learn the janggu and sing too.
Make a lively rhythm with the janggu.
In samulnori, people dance to the janggu.

explain: 한국 전통 악기로, 가운데가 잘록한 모양의 북이에요. 양쪽 면을 쳐서 소리를 내요. 사물놀이에서 쓰는 악기 중 하나예요.

phrases.en: I am learning how to play the janggu.
phrases.nuance_en: Drum-like instruments use the verb 치다.

phrases.en: I can hear the janggu sound from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기가 내는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sound the instrument makes.

phrases.en: We danced to the janggu rhythm.
phrases.nuance_en: 장단 is the rhythm pattern of Korean music.

explain_en: It is a traditional Korean drum with a narrow waist in the middle. You hit both sides to make sound. It is one of the instruments used in samulnori.

examples.en: My older brother plays the clarinet in the school band.
I like the clarinet because its sound is soft.
A clarinet makes sound when you blow into it with your mouth.
The new clarinet arrived, and I started practicing.
I tried playing movie music on the clarinet.

examples.ko: 클라리넷도 불고 피아노도 칠 줄 아는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who can play both the clarinet and the piano.

explain: 입으로 불어서 소리를 내는 악기라 '클라리넷을 불다'라고 해요. 피아노나 기타는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'를 써요. 외래어 표기는 '클라리네트'가 아니라 '클라리넷'이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 일주일에 두 번 클라리넷을 불어요.
phrases.en: I play the clarinet twice a week.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 불다 because you blow into it.

phrases.en: I can hear the soft sound of the clarinet.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the instrument's sound.

phrases.en: I've been learning the clarinet since this year.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when studying an instrument.

explain_en: You make the sound by blowing, so you say '클라리넷을 불다'. For piano and guitar you use '치다' and for violin '켜다'. The standard spelling is 클라리넷, not '클라리네트'.

examples.ko: 핸드볼은 손으로 공을 던져 골을 넣어요.
examples.en: In handball, you throw the ball by hand to score goals.
I played handball for the first time at school.
I watched a handball match on TV.
My younger sibling says they want to be a handball player.
Handball has goals like soccer does.

examples.ko: 체육 시간에 핸드볼로 반 대항전을 했어요.
examples.en: In gym class we had a handball match between classes.

explain: 스포츠 종목 이름이에요. 축구에서 손으로 공을 건드리는 반칙도 '핸드볼'이라고 해서 '핸드볼 반칙'이라고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I watched a handball game in the evening.
phrases.nuance_en: 경기 refers to a match.

phrases.en: My friend is a handball player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 핸드볼을 하는 선수를 말해요. 학교나 팀에서 뛰는 사람에게도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone who plays handball on a team, at school or professionally.

phrases.en: We played handball in PE class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 이름 뒤에 '하다'를 붙여 그 운동을 한다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 after a sport's name means to play it.

explain_en: It is the name of a sport. In soccer, touching the ball with the hand is also called 핸드볼, so people sometimes say '핸드볼 반칙' (handball foul).
